newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BLACK REMAINS ANGRY AT SELECTORS BUT NOT DOWNHEARTED.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BLACK REMAINS ANGRY AT SELECTORS BUT NOT DOWNHEARTED.

text.p: Olympic 400 metres silver medallist Roger Black remained angry but not downhearted at his treatment by the British selectors on the eve of the sixth world championships on Friday.
Black, who missed the British trials because of a virus, will run the 4x400 metres relay only here after failing to win selection as one of the trio to contest the individual 400.
"I was down three or four weeks ago but I've dealt with it," he told a news conference. "If I'd let it get to me I wouldn't have come out here.
"I have two roles to play. Firstly, as British team captain and secondly as part of the 400 metres relay team fighting for a gold medal."
Black was optimistic about the British team prospects.
"We've got Kelly Holmes and Jonathan Edwards who should win gold if everything goes to plan." he said.
"Others who should be in contention include Denise Lewis, Steve Backley, who always raises his game, and the 400 metres relay boys."
Black added he was still not 100 percent fit after his recent bout of illness but said at the moment he felt he could still be a member of the relay squad.
"I have more good days than bad days. I'd say I'm at about 85 or 90 percent fitness," he said.
Black, second to Michael Johnson in Atlanta, said he thought his compatriot Iwan Thomas could provide the shock of the championships by beating the American to the line in the 400.
Johnson has struggled with injury problems since he failed to finish the 150 metres race against Donovan Bailey in Toronto on June 1.
He was recently given a wild card to compete in Athens after missing the US championships, which were mandatory for selection to the American team.
"We shall have a good indication of the shape of Michael Johnson after the semifinals," Black said. "If he's struggling, Iwan could be in with a very good chance."
